periods.market_context: The equity market showed a lack of activity, frustrating short-term investors. The UK equity market traded sideways for almost forty weeks in a range of only 7%, reminiscent of the 'flatliner' market of October 2001 to May 2002. High-risk trades (mining, technology, emerging markets) were down year-to-date. The global economy was described as 'treading a tightrope between deflation and reflation'. After a long period of sideways trading, there was common complacency, which could be problematic at a seasonally difficult time for markets.
periods.thesis: As long-term investors, directionless markets are less of a problem; patience is key. The investment approach focuses on good stock picking, active asset allocation (in and out of equities) at the right time, and a focus on dividend income, which should thrive in such an environment. Although advocating low portfolio turnover, there will be times to be active. The Fund's asset allocation and stock selection reflect the uncertain outcome between deflation and reflation, with holdings in bonds and preference shares for slower growth/disinflation, cash and short-dated gilts for flexibility and capital protection, and equity holdings biased towards consumer goods and utilities for performance in either scenario.
periods.decisions_taken: Added one new holding: Reynolds American, following its merger with Brown & Williamson. The rationale was based on revised upward cost savings (over $550m expected next year) and a commitment to a 75% payout ratio, offering a prospective dividend yield of over 9%.
periods.observed_outcome: The Reynolds American stock rose from $66 (purchase price) to $76. The overall Trojan Fund performance for the three months ending 31 July 2004 was +0.24%.
